import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.30

by H. Lausch

Let $\mathfrak{X}$, $\mathfrak{Y}$ be Fitting classes of soluble groups which satisfy the
Lockett condition, i.e. $\mathfrak{X} \cap \mathfrak{S}_* = \mathfrak{X}_*$,
$\mathfrak{Y} \cap \mathfrak{S}_* = \mathfrak{Y}_*$, where $\mathfrak{S}$ denotes the Fitting
class of all soluble groups and the lower star the bottom of the Lockett section determined by
the given Fitting class. Does $\mathfrak{X} \cap \mathfrak{Y}$ satisfy the Lockett condition?

Editors' comment (2001): the answer is affirmative if $\mathfrak{X}$ and $\mathfrak{Y}$ are
local (A. Grytczuk, N. T. Vorob'ev, *Tsukuba J. Math.* **18**, no. 1 (1994), 63–67).

## Conventions

As usual in the theory of Fitting classes (and in Lockett's work), "group" means finite group,
and the universe is the class $\mathfrak{S}$ of all finite soluble groups. A class of groups is
a set of bundled groups (`GrpCat`), and all notions are isomorphism invariant.

* A *Fitting class* is a nonempty, isomorphism closed class $\mathfrak{X} \subseteq \mathfrak{S}$
  which is closed under normal subgroups and under products of two normal subgroups.
* The *$\mathfrak{X}$-radical* $G_{\mathfrak{X}}$ of a group $G$ is the join (product) of all
  normal subgroups of $G$ belonging to $\mathfrak{X}$; for a Fitting class $\mathfrak{X}$ and a
  finite group $G$ it is the largest normal $\mathfrak{X}$-subgroup of $G$.
* A Fitting class $\mathfrak{X}$ is a *Lockett class* if
  $(G \times H)_{\mathfrak{X}} = G_{\mathfrak{X}} \times H_{\mathfrak{X}}$ for all $G, H$.
* The *Lockett closure* $\mathfrak{X}^*$ of a Fitting class $\mathfrak{X}$ is the smallest
  Lockett class containing $\mathfrak{X}$ (Lockett, 1974); we define it as the intersection of
  all Lockett classes containing $\mathfrak{X}$.
* The *Lockett section* of $\mathfrak{X}$ is the set of all Fitting classes $\mathfrak{Y}$ with
  $\mathfrak{Y}^* = \mathfrak{X}^*$, and $\mathfrak{X}_*$ is its bottom element, i.e. the
  intersection of all Fitting classes in the Lockett section of $\mathfrak{X}$.
* $\mathfrak{X}$ *satisfies the Lockett condition* (Lockett's conjecture holds for
  $\mathfrak{X}$) if $\mathfrak{X} \cap \mathfrak{S}_* = \mathfrak{X}_*$. Lockett conjectured
  that every Fitting class of finite soluble groups satisfies this; Berger and Cossey (1978)
  gave a counterexample.
* Following Hartley (1969), a Fitting class $\mathfrak{X}$ is *local* if
  $\mathfrak{X} = LR(f) = \mathfrak{S}_\pi \cap \bigcap_{p \in \pi}
  f(p)\,\mathfrak{S}_p\,\mathfrak{S}_{p'}$ for some Hartley function $f$, i.e. a function
  assigning to each prime $p$ a Fitting class $f(p)$ or the empty class, where
  $\pi = \{p : f(p) \neq \emptyset\}$ is the support of $f$ and juxtaposition denotes the
  Fitting product $\mathfrak{X}\mathfrak{Y} = (G : G/G_{\mathfrak{X}} \in \mathfrak{Y})$.

*References:*
* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 8.30.
* F. P. Lockett, *The Fitting class $\mathfrak{F}^*$*, Math. Z. **137** (1974), 131–136.
* B. Hartley, *On Fischer's dualization of formation theory*, Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) **19**
  (1969), 193–207.
* A. Grytczuk, N. T. Vorob'ev, *On Lockett's conjecture for finite groups*, Tsukuba J. Math.
  **18**, no. 1 (1994), 63–67.
* K. Doerk, T. Hawkes, *Finite Soluble Groups*, de Gruyter, 1992, Chapters IX and X.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.30»

/-- A class of (finite) groups: a set of bundled groups. -/
abbrev GroupClass := Set GrpCat.{0}

/-- The class $\mathfrak{S}$ of all finite soluble groups. -/
def solubleGroups : GroupClass := {G | Finite G ∧ IsSolvable G}

local notation "𝔖" => solubleGroups

/-- The $\mathfrak{X}$-radical $G_{\mathfrak{X}}$ of a group $G$: the join of all normal
subgroups of $G$ that belong to the class $\mathfrak{X}$. When $\mathfrak{X}$ is a Fitting class
and $G$ is finite, this is the largest normal $\mathfrak{X}$-subgroup of $G$. -/
def radical (𝔛 : GroupClass) (G : Type) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  sSup {N : Subgroup G | N.Normal ∧ GrpCat.of N ∈ 𝔛}

/-- The radical is a normal subgroup, being a join of normal subgroups. -/
instance radical_normal (𝔛 : GroupClass) (G : Type) [Group G] : (radical 𝔛 G).Normal := by
  refine Subgroup.Normal.of_conjugate_fixed fun g => ?_
  rw [radical, sSup_eq_iSup', Subgroup.pointwise_smul_def, Subgroup.map_iSup]
  refine iSup_congr fun N => ?_
  rw [← Subgroup.pointwise_smul_def]
  exact @Subgroup.Normal.conj_smul_eq_self _ _ g N N.2.1

/-- A *Fitting class* (of finite soluble groups): a nonempty, isomorphism closed class of finite
soluble groups that is closed under taking normal subgroups and under products of two normal
subgroups. -/
structure IsFittingClass (𝔛 : GroupClass) : Prop where
  /-- The universe: every member of the class is a finite soluble group. -/
  subset_soluble : 𝔛 ⊆ 𝔖
  /-- The class is nonempty. -/
  nonempty : 𝔛.Nonempty
  /-- The class is closed under isomorphisms. -/
  iso_closed : ∀ {G H : GrpCat.{0}}, (G ≃* H) → G ∈ 𝔛 → H ∈ 𝔛
  /-- The class is closed under normal subgroups. -/
  normal_closed : ∀ (G : GrpCat.{0}) (N : Subgroup G), N.Normal → G ∈ 𝔛 → GrpCat.of N ∈ 𝔛
  /-- The class is closed under products of two normal subgroups: if $G = N_1 N_2$ with
  $N_1, N_2 \trianglelefteq G$ and $N_1, N_2 \in \mathfrak{X}$, then $G \in \mathfrak{X}$. -/
  normal_prod_closed : ∀ (G : GrpCat.{0}) (N₁ N₂ : Subgroup G), N₁.Normal → N₂.Normal →
    GrpCat.of N₁ ∈ 𝔛 → GrpCat.of N₂ ∈ 𝔛 → N₁ ⊔ N₂ = ⊤ → G ∈ 𝔛

/-- A *Lockett class*: a Fitting class $\mathfrak{X}$ such that
$(G \times H)_{\mathfrak{X}} = G_{\mathfrak{X}} \times H_{\mathfrak{X}}$ for all finite soluble
groups $G$ and $H$. -/
def IsLockettClass (𝔛 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  IsFittingClass 𝔛 ∧ ∀ G H : GrpCat.{0}, G ∈ 𝔖 → H ∈ 𝔖 →
    radical 𝔛 (G × H) = (radical 𝔛 G).prod (radical 𝔛 H)

/-- The *Lockett closure* $\mathfrak{X}^*$ of a class $\mathfrak{X}$: the intersection of all
Lockett classes containing $\mathfrak{X}$. By Lockett's theorem, for a Fitting class
$\mathfrak{X}$ this is the smallest Fitting class $\mathfrak{X}^*$ containing $\mathfrak{X}$ with
$(G \times H)_{\mathfrak{X}^*} = G_{\mathfrak{X}^*} \times H_{\mathfrak{X}^*}$ for all $G, H$. -/
def lockettStar (𝔛 : GroupClass) : GroupClass :=
  ⋂₀ {𝔜 : GroupClass | IsLockettClass 𝔜 ∧ 𝔛 ⊆ 𝔜}

/-- The *Lockett section* of $\mathfrak{X}$: the set of all Fitting classes $\mathfrak{Y}$ with
$\mathfrak{Y}^* = \mathfrak{X}^*$. -/
def lockettSection (𝔛 : GroupClass) : Set GroupClass :=
  {𝔜 | IsFittingClass 𝔜 ∧ lockettStar 𝔜 = lockettStar 𝔛}

/-- The bottom $\mathfrak{X}_*$ of the Lockett section of $\mathfrak{X}$: the intersection of all
Fitting classes $\mathfrak{Y}$ with $\mathfrak{Y}^* = \mathfrak{X}^*$. By Lockett's theorem, this
intersection again lies in the Lockett section, so it is its smallest element. -/
def lockettLower (𝔛 : GroupClass) : GroupClass :=
  ⋂₀ lockettSection 𝔛

/-- A class $\mathfrak{X}$ *satisfies the Lockett condition* if
$\mathfrak{X} \cap \mathfrak{S}_* = \mathfrak{X}_*$, where $\mathfrak{S}$ is the class of all
finite soluble groups. -/
def SatisfiesLockettCondition (𝔛 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  𝔛 ∩ lockettLower 𝔖 = lockettLower 𝔛

/-- A Lockett class is its own Lockett closure. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem lockettStar_eq_self {𝔛 : GroupClass} (h : IsLockettClass 𝔛) : lockettStar 𝔛 = 𝔛 := by
  refine (Set.sInter_subset_of_mem ?_).antisymm (Set.subset_sInter fun _ h𝔜 => h𝔜.2)
  exact ⟨h, subset_rfl⟩

/-- A class is contained in its Lockett closure. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem subset_lockettStar (𝔛 : GroupClass) : 𝔛 ⊆ lockettStar 𝔛 :=
  Set.subset_sInter fun _ h𝔜 => h𝔜.2

/-- A Fitting class belongs to its own Lockett section. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_lockettSection_self {𝔛 : GroupClass} (h : IsFittingClass 𝔛) :
    𝔛 ∈ lockettSection 𝔛 :=
  ⟨h, rfl⟩

/-- The bottom of the Lockett section of a Fitting class $\mathfrak{X}$ is contained in
$\mathfrak{X}$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem lockettLower_subset {𝔛 : GroupClass} (h : IsFittingClass 𝔛) : lockettLower 𝔛 ⊆ 𝔛 :=
  Set.sInter_subset_of_mem (mem_lockettSection_self h)

/--
Let $\mathfrak{X}$, $\mathfrak{Y}$ be Fitting classes of soluble groups which satisfy the
Lockett condition, i.e. $\mathfrak{X} \cap \mathfrak{S}_* = \mathfrak{X}_*$,
$\mathfrak{Y} \cap \mathfrak{S}_* = \mathfrak{Y}_*$, where $\mathfrak{S}$ denotes the Fitting
class of all soluble groups and the lower star the bottom of the Lockett section determined by
the given Fitting class. Does $\mathfrak{X} \cap \mathfrak{Y}$ satisfy the Lockett condition?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.30» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ 𝔛 𝔜 : GroupClass, IsFittingClass 𝔛 → IsFittingClass 𝔜 →
      SatisfiesLockettCondition 𝔛 → SatisfiesLockettCondition 𝔜 →
      SatisfiesLockettCondition (𝔛 ∩ 𝔜) := by
  sorry

/-- The class $\mathfrak{S}_\pi$ of all finite soluble $\pi$-groups, for a set $\pi$ of primes:
the finite soluble groups whose order is divisible only by primes in $\pi$. In particular
$\mathfrak{S}_{\{p\}} = \mathfrak{S}_p$ is the class of finite $p$-groups and
$\mathfrak{S}_{\{p\}^c} = \mathfrak{S}_{p'}$ is the class of finite soluble $p'$-groups. -/
def piGroups (π : Set Nat.Primes) : GroupClass :=
  {G | G ∈ 𝔖 ∧ ∀ p : Nat.Primes, (p : ℕ) ∣ Nat.card G → p ∈ π}

/-- The *Fitting product* $\mathfrak{X}\mathfrak{Y}$ of two classes: the class of all groups $G$
with $G / G_{\mathfrak{X}} \in \mathfrak{Y}$. -/
def fittingProduct (𝔛 𝔜 : GroupClass) : GroupClass :=
  {G | GrpCat.of (G ⧸ radical 𝔛 G) ∈ 𝔜}

/-- The support $\{p : f(p) \neq \emptyset\}$ of a function $f$ from the primes to classes of
groups. -/
def hartleySupport (f : Nat.Primes → GroupClass) : Set Nat.Primes :=
  {p | (f p).Nonempty}

/-- A *Hartley function* ($H$-function): a function assigning to each prime $p$ either the empty
class or a Fitting class $f(p)$. -/
def IsHartleyFunction (f : Nat.Primes → GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∀ p, (f p).Nonempty → IsFittingClass (f p)

/-- The class $LR(f) = \mathfrak{S}_\pi \cap \bigcap_{p \in \pi} f(p)\,\mathfrak{S}_p\,
\mathfrak{S}_{p'}$ locally defined by a Hartley function $f$ with support $\pi$ (Hartley, 1969).
Here $f(p)\,\mathfrak{S}_p\,\mathfrak{S}_{p'}$ is the Fitting product, i.e. the class of finite
soluble groups $G$ such that $G / G_{f(p)\mathfrak{S}_p}$ is a $p'$-group, where
$G_{f(p)\mathfrak{S}_p}$ is the largest normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ with $N / N_{f(p)}$ a
$p$-group. -/
def locallyDefined (f : Nat.Primes → GroupClass) : GroupClass :=
  piGroups (hartleySupport f) ∩
    ⋂ p ∈ hartleySupport f, fittingProduct (fittingProduct (f p) (piGroups {p})) (piGroups {p}ᶜ)

/-- A class of groups is a *local Fitting class* if it is of the form $LR(f)$ for some Hartley
function $f$. -/
def IsLocalFittingClass (𝔛 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : Nat.Primes → GroupClass, IsHartleyFunction f ∧ 𝔛 = locallyDefined f

/--
Editors' comment (2001): the answer to Problem 8.30 is affirmative if $\mathfrak{X}$ and
$\mathfrak{Y}$ are local. That is, if $\mathfrak{X}$, $\mathfrak{Y}$ are local Fitting classes
of finite soluble groups satisfying the Lockett condition
$\mathfrak{X} \cap \mathfrak{S}_* = \mathfrak{X}_*$, $\mathfrak{Y} \cap \mathfrak{S}_* =
\mathfrak{Y}_*$, then $\mathfrak{X} \cap \mathfrak{Y}$ satisfies the Lockett condition
(A. Grytczuk, N. T. Vorob'ev, *Tsukuba J. Math.* **18**, no. 1 (1994), 63–67).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.30».variants.local :
    ∀ 𝔛 𝔜 : GroupClass, IsFittingClass 𝔛 → IsFittingClass 𝔜 →
      IsLocalFittingClass 𝔛 → IsLocalFittingClass 𝔜 →
      SatisfiesLockettCondition 𝔛 → SatisfiesLockettCondition 𝔜 →
      SatisfiesLockettCondition (𝔛 ∩ 𝔜) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.30»
attempts.decomposition_objections: No substantive objection. One clarification for the variant slot: the notes describe local Fitting classes by a formula of the shape '⋂_p S_{p'} ∘ f(p) ∘ S_p', which is the formation-style shape. The Hartley/Vorob'ev definition of a local Fitting class (the one used by Grytczuk–Vorob'ev) is the dual LR(f) = 𝔖_π ∩ ⋂_{p∈π} f(p)𝔖_p𝔖_{p'} with the Fitting product 𝔛𝔜 = (G : G/G_𝔛 ∈ 𝔜) and π = Supp f; the file uses this form, as the notes' 'style … must be formalized carefully' seems to intend.
modeling_decisions: A class of groups is a `Set GrpCat.{0}` (bundled groups in `Type`); every finite group is isomorphic to one in `Type`, so no generality is lost. Isomorphism closure is a field of `IsFittingClass`, so all class-theoretic notions are only meaningful up to isomorphism, as in the literature.

Universe: following Lockett's paper and the notebook's 'soluble group' convention, `IsFittingClass` bakes in `𝔛 ⊆ 𝔖` where `𝔖 = solubleGroups = {G | Finite G ∧ IsSolvable G}`. The Lockett-class property is quantified over G, H ∈ 𝔖 only. (Quantifying over all finite groups would be equivalent since 𝔛 ⊆ 𝔖.)

`IsFittingClass` requires nonemptiness (per the decomposition notes), isomorphism closure, closure under normal subgroups, and closure under products of two normal subgroups in the form `N₁ ⊔ N₂ = ⊤ → G ∈ 𝔛` (the standard N₀-closure for two normal subgroups; equivalent to the `N₁N₂ ∈ 𝔛` form given iso- and sₙ-closure).

The radical `radical 𝔛 G` is defined as `sSup` of the normal subgroups belonging to 𝔛. For a Fitting class and a finite group this is exactly the largest normal 𝔛-subgroup (the set is finite, contains ⊥, and is closed under joins by N₀-closure). It is proved normal in the file (`radical_normal`), which is needed to form the quotient in the Fitting product.

The Lockett closure 𝔛^* is defined as the intersection of all Lockett classes (Fitting classes 𝔜 ⊆ 𝔖 with (G×H)_𝔜 = G_𝔜 × H_𝔜 for all finite soluble G, H) containing 𝔛, i.e. as the smallest Lockett class containing 𝔛. This is the characterization given in the decomposition notes; it agrees with Lockett's original construction by Lockett's theorem (𝔉 ⊆ 𝔉^*, 𝔉^* is a Lockett class, and 𝔉 ⊆ 𝔊 ⟹ 𝔉^* ⊆ 𝔊^* = 𝔊 for Lockett 𝔊). Reviewers should confirm they accept this equivalent definition instead of the (G×G)_𝔉 construction.

The Lockett section of 𝔛 is `{𝔜 | IsFittingClass 𝔜 ∧ lockettStar 𝔜 = lockettStar 𝔛}` and 𝔛_* is its intersection `⋂₀`. Lockett proved this intersection again lies in the section, so it is the bottom element; the file relies on that theorem rather than restating it.
The Lockett condition is stated literally as the set equation `𝔛 ∩ lockettLower 𝔖 = lockettLower 𝔛`.

Local Fitting classes follow Hartley (1969) in the form used by Vorob'ev and Grytczuk–Vorob'ev: a Hartley function assigns to each prime a Fitting class or ∅ (`IsHartleyFunction`), π = Supp f, and `locallyDefined f = piGroups π ∩ ⋂_{p∈π} fittingProduct (fittingProduct (f p) (piGroups {p})) (piGroups {p}ᶜ)`, i.e. LR(f) = 𝔖_π ∩ ⋂_{p∈π} f(p)𝔖_p𝔖_{p'} where the Fitting product is 𝔛𝔜 = (G : G/G_𝔛 ∈ 𝔜). The product is parenthesised as (f(p)𝔖_p)𝔖_{p'}; the Fitting product is associative so this is immaterial. This is the point a reviewer should check most carefully (product order f(p)·𝔖_p·𝔖_{p'} and the support convention 𝔖_π ∩ …), since the decomposition notes only give the shape '⋂_p S_{p'} ∘ f(p) ∘ S_p style'.
p-groups and p'-groups are defined via prime divisors of `Nat.card` inside the finite soluble universe (`piGroups π`), rather than via `IsPGroup`; for finite groups these agree.

The variant theorem keeps the explicit `IsFittingClass 𝔛`/`IsFittingClass 𝔜` hypotheses alongside `IsLocalFittingClass`; they are redundant (LR(f) is always a Fitting class) but harmless and match the wording 'Fitting classes … which are local'.

Four short `@[category API]` lemmas with proofs (`lockettStar_eq_self`, `subset_lockettStar`, `mem_lockettSection_self`, `lockettLower_subset`) are included as basic sanity checks of the bespoke definitions, as CONTRIBUTING.md asks for bespoke definitions.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.30

by H. Lausch

Let $\mathfrak X$ and $\mathfrak Y$ be Fitting classes of finite soluble groups satisfying the
Lockett condition. Does $\mathfrak X \cap \mathfrak Y$ satisfy the Lockett condition?

The editors report that the answer is affirmative when $\mathfrak X$ and $\mathfrak Y$ are local
Fitting classes, citing A. Grytczuk and N. T. Vorob'ev, *Tsukuba J. Math.* **18** (1994), 63--67.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook, Problem 8.30](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.30»

/-- A bundled finite group. This lets a Fitting class range over finite groups up to isomorphism. -/
structure FiniteGroup where
  carrier : Type
  group : Group carrier
  finite : Finite carrier

attribute [instance] FiniteGroup.group FiniteGroup.finite

/-- A class of finite groups. -/
abbrev GroupClass := FiniteGroup → Prop

/-- The finite group carried by a subgroup of a bundled finite group. -/
def FiniteGroup.subgroup (G : FiniteGroup) (H : Subgroup G.carrier) : FiniteGroup where
  carrier := H
  group := inferInstance
  finite := inferInstance

/-- The direct product of two bundled finite groups. -/
def FiniteGroup.prod (G H : FiniteGroup) : FiniteGroup where
  carrier := G.carrier × H.carrier
  group := inferInstance
  finite := inferInstance

/-- The quotient of a bundled finite group by a normal subgroup. -/
def FiniteGroup.quotient (G : FiniteGroup) (N : Subgroup G.carrier) (hN : N.Normal) :
    FiniteGroup := by
  letI : N.Normal := hN
  exact {
    carrier := G.carrier ⧸ N
    group := inferInstance
    finite := inferInstance }

/-- Pointwise inclusion of classes of finite groups. -/
def ClassLE (X Y : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∀ G, X G → Y G

/-- Pointwise intersection of classes of finite groups. -/
def classInter (X Y : GroupClass) : GroupClass :=
  fun G ↦ X G ∧ Y G

/--
A Fitting class of finite groups: it is nonempty and closed under isomorphisms, normal subgroups,
and products of normal subgroups.
-/
def IsFittingClass (X : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  (∃ G, X G) ∧
  (∀ G H, X G → Nonempty (G.carrier ≃* H.carrier) → X H) ∧
  (∀ (G : FiniteGroup) (N : Subgroup G.carrier), X G → N.Normal → X (G.subgroup N)) ∧
  (∀ (G : FiniteGroup) (N M : Subgroup G.carrier), N.Normal → M.Normal →
    X (G.subgroup N) → X (G.subgroup M) → X (G.subgroup (N ⊔ M)))

/-- The $X$-radical of a finite group: the join of its normal $X$-subgroups. -/
def radical (X : GroupClass) (G : FiniteGroup) : Subgroup G.carrier :=
  sSup {N : Subgroup G.carrier | N.Normal ∧ X (G.subgroup N)}

/-- A class has direct-product radicals if the radical of a product is the product of radicals. -/
def HasDirectProductRadicals (X : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∀ G H, radical X (G.prod H) = (radical X G).prod (radical X H)

/--
The Lockett closure $X^*$ is the smallest Fitting class containing $X$ whose radicals commute
with finite direct products.
-/
def lockettClosure (X : GroupClass) : GroupClass :=
  fun G ↦ ∀ Y, IsFittingClass Y → ClassLE X Y → HasDirectProductRadicals Y → Y G

/--
The lower star $X_*$ is the bottom of the Lockett section consisting of the Fitting classes $Y$
with $Y^* = X^*$.
-/
def lowerStar (X : GroupClass) : GroupClass :=
  fun G ↦ ∀ Y, IsFittingClass Y → lockettClosure Y = lockettClosure X → Y G

/-- The Fitting class $\mathfrak S$ of all finite soluble groups. -/
def solubleClass : GroupClass :=
  fun G ↦ IsSolvable G.carrier

/-- A Fitting class all of whose members are soluble. -/
def IsSolubleFittingClass (X : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  IsFittingClass X ∧ ClassLE X solubleClass

/-- The Lockett condition $X \cap \mathfrak S_* = X_*$. -/
def SatisfiesLockettCondition (X : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  classInter X (lowerStar solubleClass) = lowerStar X

/-- The product $X \circ Y$ of Fitting classes, defined using the $X$-radical. -/
def classProduct (X Y : GroupClass) : GroupClass :=
  fun G ↦ ∃ (N : Subgroup G.carrier) (hN : N.Normal),
    N = radical X G ∧ Y (G.quotient N hN)

/-- The class $\mathfrak S_p$ of finite soluble $p$-groups. -/
def solublePClass (p : ℕ) : GroupClass :=
  fun G ↦ IsSolvable G.carrier ∧ IsPGroup p G.carrier

/-- The class $\mathfrak S_{p'}$ of finite soluble groups whose order is prime to $p$. -/
def solublePComplementClass (p : ℕ) : GroupClass :=
  fun G ↦ IsSolvable G.carrier ∧ ¬p ∣ Nat.card G.carrier

/--
A local Fitting class is one defined by a Hartley function $f$ via
$X = \bigcap_p \mathfrak S_{p'} \circ f(p) \circ \mathfrak S_p$, where $p$ ranges over primes.
-/
def IsLocalFittingClass (X : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  IsFittingClass X ∧ ∃ f : ℕ → GroupClass,
    (∀ p, p.Prime → IsFittingClass (f p)) ∧
    X = fun G ↦ ∀ p, p.Prime →
      classProduct (classProduct (solublePComplementClass p) (f p)) (solublePClass p) G

/--
Let $\mathfrak X$ and $\mathfrak Y$ be Fitting classes of finite soluble groups which satisfy
$\mathfrak X \cap \mathfrak S_* = \mathfrak X_*$ and
$\mathfrak Y \cap \mathfrak S_* = \mathfrak Y_*$. Does $\mathfrak X \cap \mathfrak Y$ satisfy
$(\mathfrak X \cap \mathfrak Y) \cap \mathfrak S_* = (\mathfrak X \cap \mathfrak Y)_*$?
Here the lower star denotes the bottom of the Lockett section determined by the class.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.30» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ X Y : GroupClass,
      IsSolubleFittingClass X → IsSolubleFittingClass Y →
      SatisfiesLockettCondition X → SatisfiesLockettCondition Y →
      SatisfiesLockettCondition (classInter X Y) := by
  sorry

/--
The answer to Problem 8.30 is affirmative if $\mathfrak X$ and $\mathfrak Y$ are local Fitting
classes of finite soluble groups: if both satisfy the Lockett condition, then so does
$\mathfrak X \cap \mathfrak Y$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem variants.local :
    ∀ X Y : GroupClass,
      IsSolubleFittingClass X → IsSolubleFittingClass Y →
      IsLocalFittingClass X → IsLocalFittingClass Y →
      SatisfiesLockettCondition X → SatisfiesLockettCondition Y →
      SatisfiesLockettCondition (classInter X Y) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.30»

A Fitting class is modeled as a nonempty, isomorphism-closed predicate on bundled finite groups, closed under normal subgroups and joins (products) of normal subgroups in a common ambient finite group.

The class radical is the supremum of all normal subgroups belonging to the class. The Lockett closure is defined pointwise as the intersection of all direct-product-radical Fitting classes containing the given class.
The lower star is defined as the pointwise intersection of all Fitting classes in the same Lockett section, i.e. all classes having the same Lockett closure.
The Lockett condition is stated literally as `X ∩ S_* = X_*`, where `S` is the class of all finite soluble groups.

Locality uses a Hartley function on primes and the formula `⋂ p, S_{p'} ∘ f(p) ∘ S_p`; the displayed iterated class product is left-associated. Class product is defined by quotienting by the radical of its left factor.

by H. Lausch

Lockett condition, i.e. $\mathfrak{X} \cap \mathfrak{S}_* = \mathfrak{X}_*$,
$\mathfrak{Y} \cap \mathfrak{S}_* = \mathfrak{Y}_*$, where $\mathfrak{S}$ denotes the Fitting

the given Fitting class. Does $\mathfrak{X} \cap \mathfrak{Y}$ satisfy the Lockett condition?

local (A. Grytczuk, N. T. Vorob'ev, *Tsukuba J. Math.* **18**, no. 1 (1994), 63–67).

and under products of normal subgroups. For a Fitting class $\mathfrak{X}$ and a group $G$, the
$\mathfrak{X}$-radical $G_{\mathfrak{X}}$ is the largest normal $\mathfrak{X}$-subgroup of $G$.

  $(G \times H)_{\mathfrak{X}} = G_{\mathfrak{X}} \times H_{\mathfrak{X}}$ for all $G$, $H$.
* The *Lockett closure* $\mathfrak{X}^*$ is the smallest Lockett class containing
  $\mathfrak{X}$ (Lockett); equivalently, the intersection of all Lockett classes containing
  $\mathfrak{X}$.
* The *Lockett section* of $\mathfrak{X}$ is the set of Fitting classes $\mathfrak{Y}$ with
  $\mathfrak{Y}^* = \mathfrak{X}^*$; its bottom element $\mathfrak{X}_*$ (the *lower star*) is
  the intersection of all such $\mathfrak{Y}$.

  $\mathfrak{X} \cap \mathfrak{S}_* = \mathfrak{X}_*$. Lockett conjectured that every Fitting
  class of finite soluble groups satisfies it; this was refuted by Berger and Cossey.

/-- A class of groups, represented as a predicate on groups. -/
abbrev GroupClass : Type 1 := (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop

/-- A class of groups `𝔛` is a *Fitting class of finite soluble groups* if it consists of finite
soluble groups, is nonempty, is closed under isomorphisms, is closed under taking normal
subgroups, and is closed under products of normal subgroups: if `G = N₁N₂` with `N₁`, `N₂`
normal subgroups of `G` lying in `𝔛`, then `G ∈ 𝔛`. -/
structure IsFittingClass (𝔛 : GroupClass) : Prop where
  finite_isSolvable : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝔛 G → Finite G ∧ IsSolvable G
  nonempty : ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), 𝔛 G
  of_mulEquiv : ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H], G ≃* H → 𝔛 G → 𝔛 H
  of_normal : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (N : Subgroup G), N.Normal → 𝔛 G → 𝔛 N
  of_sup_eq_top : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (N₁ N₂ : Subgroup G), N₁.Normal → N₂.Normal →

def inter (𝔛 𝔜 : GroupClass) : GroupClass :=

/-- The class `𝔖` of all finite soluble groups. -/

/-- The `𝔛`-radical `G_𝔛` of a group `G`: the join of all normal subgroups of `G` lying in `𝔛`.

  sSup {N : Subgroup G | N.Normal ∧ 𝔛 N}

/-- A Fitting class `𝔛` of finite soluble groups is a *Lockett class* if
`(G × H)_𝔛 = G_𝔛 × H_𝔛` for all finite soluble groups `G` and `H`. -/
def IsLockettClass (𝔛 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  IsFittingClass 𝔛 ∧
    ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H] [Finite G] [Finite H] [IsSolvable G] [IsSolvable H],
      radical 𝔛 (G × H) = (radical 𝔛 G).prod (radical 𝔛 H)

/-- The *Lockett closure* `𝔛^*` of a class `𝔛`: the intersection of all Lockett classes
containing `𝔛`. For a Fitting class `𝔛` this is the smallest Lockett class containing `𝔛`. -/

  fun G _ => ∀ 𝔜 : GroupClass, IsLockettClass 𝔜 → (∀ (H : Type) [Group H], 𝔛 H → 𝔜 H) → 𝔜 G

/-- The *lower star* `𝔛_*` of a Fitting class `𝔛`: the intersection of all Fitting classes `𝔜`
with `𝔜^* = 𝔛^*`, i.e. the bottom of the Lockett section determined by `𝔛`. -/

  fun G _ => ∀ 𝔜 : GroupClass, IsFittingClass 𝔜 → lockettClosure 𝔜 = lockettClosure 𝔛 → 𝔜 G

class of all finite soluble groups. -/

  inter 𝔛 (lowerStar solubleClass) = lowerStar 𝔛

  fun _ _ h𝔜 => h𝔜 G hG

theorem lockettClosure_le (𝔛 𝔜 : GroupClass) (h𝔜 : IsLockettClass 𝔜)

  ∃ P : Sylow p G, (P : Subgroup G).Normal

groups or the empty class. -/
def IsHartleyFunction (f : ℕ → GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → IsFittingClass (f p) ∨ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], ¬ f p G

  fun G _ => Finite G ∧ IsSolvable G ∧

`IsFittingClass` encodes 'Fitting class of soluble groups' in the Kourovka/Lockett sense: every member is a finite soluble group (`Finite G ∧ IsSolvable G`), the class is nonempty, isomorphism-closed, closed under normal subgroups (S_n) and under normal products (N₀: N₁, N₂ ⊴ G in the class with N₁ ⊔ N₂ = ⊤ ⟹ G in the class).

A Lockett class is defined by the standard characterization (G × H)_𝔛 = G_𝔛 × H_𝔛 for all finite soluble G, H (Lockett: equivalent to 𝔛 = 𝔛^*). The Lockett closure 𝔛^* is then defined as the intersection of all Lockett classes containing 𝔛, matching the decomposition notes ('smallest Fitting class containing X with the direct-product radical property'); this is well-defined because 𝔖 is such a class and intersections of Lockett classes are Lockett (G_{⋂𝔜} = ⋂ G_𝔜 for finite G), and equals Lockett's 𝔉^* by his theorem that 𝔉^* is the smallest Lockett class containing 𝔉. Lockett's explicit construction via (G × G)_𝔉 was deliberately not used.

The lower star 𝔛_* is defined as the intersection of all Fitting classes 𝔜 with 𝔜^* = 𝔛^* (the standard definition of the bottom of the Lockett section Locksec(𝔛)); the text's 'bottom group' is read as 'bottom class' per the decomposition notes.

The Lockett-class property quantifies over finite soluble G, H only (the universe 𝔖 of the problem); for a Fitting class contained in 𝔖 this is equivalent to quantifying over all finite groups, since (G × H)_𝔖 = G_𝔖 × H_𝔖 and G_𝔛 = (G_𝔖)_𝔛.
